families.summary: The heavy-duty 4-roll plate bending machines for wind-tower, shipyard, pressure-vessel and pipeline work: 42 models from 6.7 ft to 20 ft that roll plate up to 3-3/8″ thick. The pinch roll and both side rolls travel on a pyramid linear path on hydraulic cylinders, so the cylinders put all their force into the plate; the top roll is driven by motor and planetary gearbox with two speeds. Three digital readouts, hydraulic roll balancing, a cone-bending device and a hydraulic tilting drop-end are standard; NC or CNC control (ESA, Italy), overhead crane, side supports and a plate ejector turn the machine into a wheel-rim or shell production line.

families.summary: The Dener XL is the hydraulic press brake most Canadian shops buy from us: a stress-relieved monoblock frame, servo-valve hydraulics at constant pressure, Y1-Y2 ram axes and an X back gauge on ball screw and linear guides, driven from a 15.6″ ESA S840 2D graphic control — the operator draws the part and the control works out the sequence, tonnage and back-gauge positions. Eighteen models from 66 US tons (60 t) × 5 ft to 661 US tons (600 t) × 20 ft on the same frame design: the 5 to 10 ft machines to 353 US tons (320 t) for job-shop sheet work, the 12, 13 and 20 ft machines to 661 US tons (600 t) with up to 26.8″ daylight, 17.7″ stroke and a 23.6″ throat on the 400 and 600-ton (363 and 544 t) sizes for deep boxes and large profiles (the 60600 sits in a pit). European-style tooling and front supports come with every machine; the options run from CNC crowning and 6-axis back gauges to angle measurement, sheet followers and robot cells, and for longer work Dener builds tandem machines — two XLs on one control bending to 60 ft and 1,800 US tons (1,633 t).

families.summary: The value-line CNC press brake: a welded, stress-relieved mono-block frame, electro-hydraulic servo synchronisation with servo valves and linear scales, a servo-driven pump that only runs while the ram moves, a Delem DA-53Tx control and a servo back gauge on ball screws — the same architecture as the European machines, built to a price that lets a small shop own a real CNC brake. Twenty-five models on one design, from 55 US tons (50 t) × 4 ft to 331 US tons (300 t) × 20 ft: the 110 and 135 t (121 and 149 US tons) × 10 ft machines are the ones most Canadian shops ask for; from 170 t (187 US tons) up the machines have 17.7 – 19.7″ throats, 7.9 – 9.8″ strokes and 18.9 – 22.4″ daylight for deep boxes, with 25 – 40 cc pumps and 13 – 21 kW servo main motors, and the 220 and 250 t (243 and 276 US tons) × 13 ft bend 3/8″ plate the full length. Delem DA-53Tx with 4+1 axes, CNC crowning and DSP laser finger protection are standard; DA-58Tx, DA-66S / 69S controls, 6-axis back gauges, sheet followers and Wila clamping are options.
features: Delem DA-53Tx 15″ touch-screen CNC control; 4 axes — Y1, Y2 (independent ram cylinders), X and R back gauge

Electro-hydraulic servo synchronisation: proportional servo valves on one integrated manifold (few pipes, few leak points) and linear scales on both sides keep the ram parallel to the table — ± 0.01 mm ram repeatability

Mild hybrid drive as standard: a servo motor and servo pump in place of the conventional motor and pump — the pump turns only while the ram moves and stops while the machine waits, loads or unloads: 40 – 60 % less energy, oil 18 – 36 °F (10 – 20 °C) cooler, much less noise for a quieter shop (about 60 dB, and silent while the ram waits), longer life for the pump, seals and valves

Motorised CNC crowning (V axis) on 110 t (121 US tons) and up: the control works out how the ram and the table deflect and sets the crowning for each bend, for the same angle along the whole part
Quick-release top-tool clamps — punches load and change from the front without tools; a segmented 2-V die and a sectioned punch set (42CrMo, HRC 47), each piece marked with its material and hardness
